so that they might find provisions for themselves and for their horses.
And at that time the army of Toghril Beg marched,
and they laid waste to the territory of Nisibis, and of Maypherqat, and of Sinjar, and of the Khabur, and of Amida;
and Zirak, its governor, was killed.
And they came again against Mosul,
and they demanded from Mu'tamid al-Dawla, the ruler of Mosul, fifty thousand dinars so that they would leave and depart.
And when he disregarded them,
they took control of the city.
And Mu'tamid al-Dawla fled through an underground gate that was on the Tigris River.
And the Ghuzz entered and plundered from his palace a great wealth worth two hundred thousand dinars;
and they divided among themselves his seventeen wives, Arab and Kurdish women,
and a multitude of maidservants.
And they also plundered the city,
except for the neighborhood of Shaharsuy (Chaharsu,
bazaar?);
for its owners gave fifteen thousand dinars in exchange for their houses.
And the fathers of the wives of the ruler also ransomed them.
And the Ghuzz left governors in Mosul and went and encamped against the city of Balad,
but they were not able to capture it.
And after a few days,
a certain Ghuzz quarreled with a youth, one of the people of Mosul,
and struck him with a spear-butt.
Then the mother of the youth,
who was a bold and talkative woman,
smeared blood upon her face
and cried out in the streets,
saying: "The Ghuzz have killed my son and my daughter!"
And she stirred up contention with her voice,
and provoked the Arabs with her words;
and they rose up against the Ghuzz and killed them.
And when those who were in Balad heard, they turned back again to Mosul,
and they killed in it two thousand old men and children.
And they remained for twelve days taking captives and killing,
and to everyone they seized they would say:
"Ransom yourself!"
And thus they took all the silver, both revealed and hidden, that was in Mosul;
and at last they made peace.
And they sent out the farmers to their villages,
and commanded them to cultivate their lands.
And after a little while Mu'tamid gathered strength,
and he assembled the Ma'addites and defeated the Ghuzz,
and inflicted a great slaughter upon them;
and those who remained fled to Azerbaijan.
And in that year, which is the year 1355
1355 of the Greeks
(1043 of our Lord?),
at the end of First Tishri,
Abu'l-Faraj the worthy Nestorian monk passed away,
an accomplished man and a philosopher.
